meta.title: Reading and influences
meta.note: The order of these links changes from time to time. Learning is rarely linear, and neither is change.

tiers.label: Start here
tiers.microCopy: A way in, not a conclusion.

items.name: Institute for Government
items.annotation: Clear, practical analysis of how government actually works, including constraints, incentives, and trade-offs.

items.name: Government Digital Service – Service Manual
items.annotation: Plain-language guidance grounded in real delivery, showing what good looks like inside complex public systems.

items.name: Nesta
items.annotation: UK-focused work on innovation, systems change, and public value, often willing to question its own assumptions.

items.name: Behavioural Insights Team
items.annotation: Applied behavioural science with real-world trials, not just theory or slogans.

tiers.label: Go deeper
tiers.microCopy: When the simple explanations stop working.

items.name: Oxford Review (open articles)
items.annotation: Evidence-based management writing that explicitly challenges intuition-led and fad-driven thinking.

items.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
items.annotation: A rare example of serious, non-hyped thinking about AI, risk, governance, and organisational responsibility.

items.name: Paul Graham – Essays
items.annotation: Long-form essays on thinking, power, and systems that reward slow reading and scepticism.

items.name: OECD – Digital Government and AI
items.annotation: International, comparative analysis of digital government and AI, useful for escaping local echo chambers.

tiers.label: Challenge your assumptions
tiers.microCopy: This may change how you see the problem.

items.name: Complexity and Management (Emergence Journal)
items.annotation: Critical review of how complexity theory has been applied to management practice, assessing its robustness beyond superficial metaphor.

items.name: AI Now Institute – Research
items.annotation: Critical work on AI, power, labour, and governance that resists the idea that technology is neutral or inevitable.

items.name: The Long Now Foundation – Essays
items.annotation: Long-term thinking about systems, responsibility, and unintended consequences.

items.name: Cory Doctorow – Pluralistic Ignorance & Tech Essays
items.annotation: Sharp, sometimes uncomfortable writing on technology, power, enshittification, and institutional failure.

items.name: Adam Curtis – Documentary essays
items.annotation: Narrative explorations of power, ideology, and unintended consequences in modern systems.

items.name: London Review of Books – Essays
items.annotation: Long-form cultural and political essays that reward patience and resist simplification.

items.name: Aeon Essays
items.annotation: Philosophical and cultural writing that often reframes familiar questions in unexpected ways.

items.name: The Atlantic – Technology & Ideas
items.annotation: Selective, long-form journalism on technology and society. Worth reading critically, not passively.
